questions.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

As we found previously, the slope is $m=-\frac{1}{3}.$

Substituting $m=-\frac{1}{3}$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=-\frac{1}{3}x+b.
$$

We now need to find the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(4,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-\frac{1}{3}x+b \\ 1 & =-(\frac{1}{3})(4)+b \\ 1 & =-\frac{4}{3}+b \\ 1+\frac{4}{3} & =b \\ b & =\frac{7}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=-\frac{1}{3}x+\frac{7}{3}.
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Our goal is to write the equation in the form 

$$
ax+by=c,
$$

where $a,b,$ and $c$ are integers with no common factors and $a\ge 0.$

We begin by moving all of the variables to the left-hand side and all of the constants to the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-\frac{1}{3}x+\frac{7}{3} \\ \frac{1}{3}x+y & =\frac{7}{3} \\ x+3y & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $a,b,$ and $c$ are integers with no common factors, and $a\ge 0.$ So, we are done!

The standard form of the line is 

$$
x+3y=7.
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other. Therefore, since $\overset{↔}{AB}$ has the slope $m=-\frac{1}{3},$ our perpendicular line must have a slope of 

$$
{m}_{1}=-\frac{1}{m}=-\frac{1}{(-\frac{1}{3})}=3.
$$

So, our perpendicular line has the slope ${m}_{1}=3$ and passes through the point $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(2,8).$ 

Finally, using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & ={m}_{1}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-8 & =3(x-2) \\ y-8 & =3x-6 \\ y & =3x+2\end{aligned}
$$
